short: Web3 URL to EVM Call Message Translation
introduction: ERC-6860 specifies the translation of an HTTP-style web3:// URL into an EVM call message, so on-chain content is reachable via human-readable names. It was proposed by Qi Zhou, Chao Pi, Sam Wilson, and Nicolas Deschildre in September 2023. The URL is parsed into a contract name, chain id, and path; the name resolves to an address, and resolveMode() on the target decides how the path becomes calldata. Note: ERC-6860 is a Draft; the specification is still under active development and may change substantially.
designPurpose: ERC-6860 was designed to give Ethereum a decentralized presentation layer so that on-chain web content can be reached without trusting an off-chain gateway. Before it, reading Web3 data relied on Web2 proxies such as dApp sites or explorers outside user control. As a corrected update to ERC-4804, it specifies an RFC 3986-compatible URL grammar in ABNF and a procedure that resolves the name, detects the resolve mode, and encodes the path as calldata, so the same URL always maps to the same EVM call.
commonUsage: The translation is implemented by Web3 URL gateways and browser extensions that let users open web3:// links to view on-chain HTML, SVG, and JSON rendered straight from contracts. In manual mode the raw path is passed as calldata and the response is treated as bytes; in auto mode a method name and typed arguments are encoded with the standard contract ABI, optionally shaped by a returns attribute. It pairs with ENS (ERC-137) for name resolution and with resource-serving contracts such as those following ERC-5219.
fn.resolveMode.desc: A read-only hook the target contract exposes so the protocol can pick a resolve mode. The bytes32 for 'manual' selects raw-path calldata, while 'auto', an empty value, zero, or a revert selects ABI-encoded auto mode.
fn.resolveMode.returns.mode: The mode selector as bytes32: 'manual' for manual mode, or 'auto' (also empty, zero, or a revert) for auto mode.
sim.urlTranslationWalkthrough.name: Web3 URL Translation Walkthrough
sim.urlTranslationWalkthrough.desc: Follow a web3:// URL as the resolver parses it, detects the contract's resolve mode, and turns it into an EVM call.
sim.urlTranslationWalkthrough.step.reque: The Web3 client requests a web3:// URL from the resolver instead of routing through a Web2 proxy.
sim.urlTranslationWalkthrough.step.parse: The resolver parses the URL into its contract name, chain id, and path, resolving the name to an address via ENS.
sim.urlTranslationWalkthrough.step.detec: The resolver calls resolveMode() on the target to choose manual or auto mode; an empty or reverting result means auto mode.
sim.urlTranslationWalkthrough.step.call: The resolver encodes the path as calldata, sends the read-only EVM call, and returns the decoded bytes to the client.
